new_misconceptions.message: When you subtract equations, you need to subtract both sides — the left-hand side AND the right-hand side; here that means 23 minus 20, giving x = 3, not x = 23.
Once you reach 5y = 11, remember to divide both sides by 5 to isolate y — the answer is y = 2.2, not 11.
When substituting x = 3 back in, 4x means 4 multiplied by 3 (which is 12), not 4 plus 3; using 12 gives 5y = 11 and y = 2.2.
The value you find by subtracting the equations is x (because the y-terms cancelled), so x = 3; substituting that back gives y = 2.2, not x = 2 and y = 3.

rationale: Original eq2 (3x + 2y = 13) was inconsistent with stored solutions [3, 2.2]: 3(3)+2(2.2)=13.4 not 13. Minimal repair: change coefficient of y in eq2 from 2 to 5 and RHS from 13 to 20, giving 3x + 5y = 20. Both equations now share the same y-coefficient (5), so subtracting eq2 from eq1 directly eliminates y: x = 3. Back-substitution: 4(3)+5y=23 => y=11/5=2.2. Stored solutions verified exactly: eq1 4(3)+5(2.2)=23 and eq2 3(3)+5(2.2)=20.
